title: Goal-Driven Multi-Agent System
description: An introduction to the Goal-Driven approach for sustaining 300+ hours of continuous multi-agent effort on complex problems.

steps.title: Welcome to Goal-Driven
steps.description: Goal-Driven is a methodology for multi-agent systems (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw) to solve extremely complex problems with specific objectives and strict criteria. It's ideal for compiler design, theorem proving, database architecture, and sophisticated system-level challenges.

steps.title: Core Concepts
steps.description: The system is built on four pillars: (1) Goal — the ultimate objective, (2) Criteria — conditions for success, (3) Subagent — the persistent worker, and (4) Master Agent — the controller and evaluator. The master agent loops: create subagent → check activity → evaluate criteria → restart if needed → stop when done.

steps.title: The Goal-Driven Loop
steps.description: The entire philosophy reduces to a simple loop: while (criteria not met) { let the subagent work }. The master agent checks subagent activity every 5 minutes, evaluates results against criteria, and restarts subagents as needed. The process never stops until criteria are satisfied or the user manually intervenes.

steps.title: Proven Results
steps.description: Goal-Driven has produced real open-source projects: a TypeScript compiler written in C++ (~100 hours of agent work) and SQLite reimplemented in Rust (~30 hours). These demonstrate the approach's power for tackling projects that would otherwise require massive human effort.
